12 copy-paste formulas for everyday work spreadsheets: lookups, totals by category, overdue tasks, clean-up and dates. Each one gave the right result on sample data when we checked it.

We entered each formula in LibreOffice Calc 25.2 on Oct 29, 2026, ran it on made-up sample data, and confirmed the result by hand. We have not run them in Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets themselves yet. The notes under each formula say which versions support it. Change the cell ranges and sheet names to match your…

Looks for A2 in the Products sheet's column A and returns the matching value from column C. Shows "Not found" instead of an error. Excel 365/2021/2024 and Google Sheets. Checked in LibreOffice Calc 25.2 on Oct 29, 2026 with fictional sample data: passed.

p.title: Find a value by ID (XLOOKUP)
p.text: =XLOOKUP(A2, Products!A:A, Products!C:C, "Not found")

docs.x: Same job as XLOOKUP, works in every Excel version and Google Sheets. Checked in LibreOffice Calc 25.2 on Oct 29, 2026 with fictional sample data: passed.

p.title: Old-school lookup (older Excel)
p.text: =IFERROR(INDEX(Products!C:C, MATCH(A2, Products!A:A, 0)), "Not found")

docs.t: Does this value exist in a list?
docs.x: Handy for checking whether a customer, SKU or email already exists. Checked in LibreOffice Calc 25.2 on Oct 29, 2026 with fictional sample data: passed.

p.title: Does this value exist in a list?
p.text: =IF(COUNTIF(List!A:A, A2)>0, "Yes", "No")

docs.x: Adds column D only where column B is "Marketing". Replace the text with a cell reference like H2 to make it reusable. Checked in LibreOffice Calc 25.2 on Oct 29, 2026 with fictional sample data: passed.

p.title: Sum by category
p.text: =SUMIFS(D:D, B:B, "Marketing")

docs.x: Due dates in E, status in F. Counts tasks past due that aren't marked Done. Checked in LibreOffice Calc 25.2 on Oct 29, 2026 with fictional sample data: passed.

p.title: Count overdue tasks
p.text: =COUNTIFS(E:E, "<"&TODAY(), F:F, "<>Done")

docs.x: Format the cell as a percentage. Column A holds task names, F holds status. Checked in LibreOffice Calc 25.2 on Oct 29, 2026 with fictional sample data: passed.

p.title: % complete
p.text: =COUNTIF(F2:F200, "Done") / COUNTA(A2:A200)

docs.x: Returns every row where column B is "Open". Updates automatically. Excel 365/2021/2024 and Google Sheets. Checked in LibreOffice Calc 25.2 on Oct 29, 2026 with fictional sample data: passed.

p.title: Show only matching rows
p.text: =FILTER(A2:F200, B2:B200="Open")

docs.x: Removes leading, trailing and double spaces, a top cause of lookups failing. Checked in LibreOffice Calc 25.2 on Oct 29, 2026 with fictional sample data: passed.

p.title: Remove extra spaces
p.text: =TRIM(A2)

docs.x: Joins A2 to D2 with commas and skips blanks. Checked in LibreOffice Calc 25.2 on Oct 29, 2026 with fictional sample data: passed.

p.title: Join cells with a separator
p.text: =TEXTJOIN(", ", TRUE, A2:D2)

docs.x: Counts Monday to Friday. Add a holiday range as a 3rd argument. Checked in LibreOffice Calc 25.2 on Oct 29, 2026 with fictional sample data: passed.

p.title: Working days between two dates
p.text: =NETWORKDAYS(B2, C2)

docs.x: Shows blank instead of #DIV/0! when C2 is empty. Checked in LibreOffice Calc 25.2 on Oct 29, 2026 with fictional sample data: passed.

p.title: Hide errors politely

a: Give the AI your rough bullet points, who it's for and the tone you want. Ask it to keep it short and put the main ask in the first two lines.
Then read it, fix any facts, and reply "shorter" or "warmer" until it sounds like you. Use placeholders like [CLIENT] instead of real names.

p.title: Write a clear email from bullet points
p.text:
Turn these notes into a clear, friendly work email to [RECIPIENT / ROLE]. Keep it under 150 words, put the main ask in the first two lines, and end with one specific next step.
Notes: [PASTE BULLETS]

more: Two more free email shortcuts: "Polite follow-up (no reply yet)" and "Push back on a deadline" are both in our free 10-prompt PDF.
Always check names, dates and numbers before you hit send.

var.gmail: In Gmail, the simplest way is to run the prompt in ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot or Claude and paste the draft into your reply. Some Google accounts also have Gemini built into Gmail; if your work account has it and your company allows it, the same prompt works there.
var.outlook: In Outlook, run the prompt in your AI chat and paste the draft back. If your company gives you Microsoft Copilot, check your AI policy, then you can use the same prompt there.

a: Paste your raw notes or the transcript and ask for a fixed structure, not just "a summary": a short summary, decisions made, action items with owner and due date, and open questions.
Check the action items against what was actually agreed, and swap names for placeholders if the notes are sensitive.

p.title: Notes to summary
p.text:
Turn these raw meeting notes into: (1) a 3-sentence summary, (2) decisions made, (3) action items as a table with owner and due date, (4) open questions.
[PASTE NOTES OR TRANSCRIPT]

more: After the meeting, the free "Follow-up email after a meeting" prompt turns that summary into a recap email.
Before you record or transcribe a call, follow your company's rules and let people know.

var.zoom: If your meeting app gives you a transcript and your company allows it, paste that transcript into the prompt. Otherwise your own bullet notes work fine.
var.teams: If Teams gives you a transcript and your company allows it, paste it into the prompt. If your company has Microsoft Copilot, check your AI policy before using it on meeting content.
var.meet: If Google Meet gives you a transcript and your company allows it, paste it into the prompt. Your own bullet notes work fine too.

guides.t: Using AI for reports and docs
a: Paste your draft or raw points, say who will read it and how much time they have, and ask for an executive summary first.
Then ask for the full structure. Check every number and quote against your source: AI can sound confident and still be wrong.

p.title: Executive summary
p.text:
Write a 5-sentence executive summary of this document for a senior leader who has 60 seconds. Lead with the conclusion and the decision needed.
[PASTE DOCUMENT]

more: Trick that helps: paste "Ask me questions first" after your request so the AI asks for missing context instead of guessing.
The Prompt Pack has more report prompts.

var.word: In Word, draft with the prompt in your AI chat and paste it in. If your company gives you Microsoft Copilot, check your AI policy first.
var.google docs: In Google Docs, draft with the prompt in your AI chat and paste it in. Some Google accounts have Gemini built into Docs; use it only if your company allows it.

a: Tell the AI which app you use and what each column holds, then ask for the formula plus a plain-English explanation.
Test it on a few rows you can check by hand before you trust it on the whole sheet. Sample rows with made-up values work fine, so you don't need to paste real data.

p.title: Write the formula for me
p.text: I use [EXCEL / GOOGLE SHEETS]. My data: column A = [WHAT], B = [WHAT], C = [WHAT], rows 2 to [N]. Write a formula for [GOAL] and explain it in plain English.

more: Or skip the AI: our formula page has copy-paste formulas for lookups, totals by category, overdue tasks and clean-up, each checked on sample data.
The Spreadsheet Kit has more formula recipes and AI prompts for Excel and Google Sheets.

var.excel: For Excel: say "I use Excel" in the prompt and mention your version if you know it, because newer functions like XLOOKUP and FILTER need Excel 365/2021 or later. Our formula page notes which versions each one needs.
var.google sheets: For Google Sheets: say "I use Google Sheets" in the prompt. Formulas like XLOOKUP and FILTER work there too; our formula page notes which apps each one needs.

a: Ask for an outline first: one full-sentence headline per slide plus a few bullets, then build or paste it into your slide app.
Give it your audience and the one thing they should remember. Then ask it to cut anything that doesn't support that point.
more: Gamma, on our tools page, can build a deck from a prompt. The Prompt Pack has presentation prompts, like turning a doc into a slide outline and writing speaker notes.

var.powerpoint: For PowerPoint: get the outline from your AI chat and paste it slide by slide. If your company gives you Microsoft Copilot, check your AI policy first.
var.google slides: For Google Slides: get the outline from your AI chat and paste it in slide by slide. Some Google accounts have Gemini built in; use it only if your company allows it.

guides.t: Using AI to write or rewrite
a: Paste what you wrote and say exactly what to change: shorter, warmer, more direct, no jargon. Tell it not to add facts.
Describe your tone once (for example "direct, warm, no jargon") and reuse it, so drafts sound like you.

p.title: Make it sound like me
p.text:
Rewrite this so it sounds like me: [DESCRIBE YOUR TONE, e.g. direct, warm, no jargon]. Don't add new facts.
[PASTE DRAFT]

more: Read the result out loud before you send it. If a sentence isn't something you'd say, change it.

a: Paste the text and say who the summary is for and how long it should be. Ask for the key points, decisions and open questions.
Ask it to quote the lines it relied on, so you can check them against the original. Don't paste confidential documents into tools your company hasn't approved.

p.title: Executive summary
p.text:
Write a 5-sentence executive summary of this document for a senior leader who has 60 seconds. Lead with the conclusion and the decision needed.
[PASTE DOCUMENT]

more: For meetings, use the "Notes to summary" prompt instead: it pulls out action items with owners and due dates.

guides.t: Using AI to plan your day
a: Brain-dump everything on your mind, then ask the AI to sort it: do today, schedule this week, delegate, drop.
You still decide. Treat its plan as a first draft and move things around.

p.title: Brain-dump to plan
p.text: Here's everything on my mind: [PASTE LIST]. Sort it into: do today, schedule this week, delegate, drop. Then give me a realistic plan for today with time blocks from [START] to [END].

more: The Prompt Pack has more planning prompts.

guides.t: Using AI for reviews and career
a: List your real wins, challenges and goals, and ask the AI to turn them into clear, specific sentences. Don't let it invent results: every claim should be something you can back up.

p.title: Self-review for performance season
p.text: Help me write my self-review. My wins: [LIST]. Challenges: [LIST]. Goals for next period: [LIST]. Make it confident, specific and honest, under 300 words.

more: The Prompt Pack has more career prompts.

a: Generic answers usually come from missing context. Say who it's for, what good looks like, the format you want and any limits.
Even easier: paste "Ask me questions first" after any request, and let the AI tell you what it needs.

p.title: Ask me questions first
p.text: Before you answer, ask me up to 5 questions about anything you need to know to do this well. Ask them all at once, then wait.

more: Then iterate: reply "shorter", "more specific" or "try again". And check everything before you use it.

guides.t: Using AI to learn something new
a: Ask it to explain the topic like you're new to it, with one everyday example, then ask it to quiz you with three questions.
For anything important, check it against an official source: AI can be confidently wrong.
more: The Prompt Pack has a set of learning prompts.

guides.t: Using AI for customer and sales messages
a: Paste the customer's message (with names and order numbers swapped for placeholders) and say the outcome you want. Ask for a calm, specific reply that answers their question first.
Never let the AI promise refunds, discounts or dates you haven't approved.

p.title: Polite follow-up (no reply yet)
p.text: Write a short, polite follow-up to [NAME] about [TOPIC]. I first emailed on [DATE]. Don't sound annoyed. Offer one easy way to answer (e.g. a yes/no or a 10-minute call).

more: The Prompt Pack has customer prompts and tough-message prompts.

a: Follow your employer's AI policy. Don't paste confidential or customer data into tools your company hasn't approved. Turning off training is not the same as your company approving the tool.
Use placeholders like [CLIENT] and [AMOUNT], and check every output before you use it.
more: The free Day 1 Starter walks you through the privacy settings in ChatGPT and Gemini, and the Cheat Sheet shows where they are.

a: ChatGPT is OpenAI's AI chat assistant, at chatgpt.com and in its phone app. The free version works with all of our prompts.
Before using it for work, check your company's AI policy and the data settings in your account.
more: Want to see what the paid plans add? The Cheat Sheet compares plans and shows where the privacy settings are, so you can decide.

a: Gemini is Google's AI assistant, at gemini.google.com and in its app. Some Google Workspace accounts also have it inside Gmail, Docs and Sheets. Our prompts work in the free version.
Use it for work data only if your company allows it.
more: The Day 1 Starter shows the Gemini privacy settings that matter.

a: Microsoft Copilot is Microsoft's AI assistant. There's a free version at copilot.microsoft.com, and some companies give staff Copilot inside Microsoft 365 apps like Outlook, Word and Teams.
If your employer provides Copilot through work, that's usually the one to use for work data. Check your AI policy.
more: Our prompts work in Copilot too: copy, fill the brackets, paste.

a: Claude is Anthropic's AI assistant, at claude.ai and in its app. Our prompts work in the free version.
As with any AI tool, check your company's policy before using it with work data.
more: Pick one assistant and stick with it for a week so you learn it properly.
